title: Outcome-driven on-prem packaging and security questionnaire interoperability experiment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a tightly scoped experiment to validate an outcome-driven packaging model for Private (VPC + on-prem) customers that simplifies procurement and reduces legal friction by pairing a predictable license fee with clearly defined support tiers and scheduled upgrade cadences, while streamlining responses to customer security questionnaires (SQs). Hypothesis: a three-tier license + ops-credit model with a documented SQ playbook and upgrade windows will increase deal velocity for mid-enterprise customers by 20% and reduce security review cycles by 30%.
proposed_pricing_matrix:
Tier A — Core Bundle: license fee = base annual fee per cluster (USD 90k), 8/5 email support, quarterly patch windows, optional ops credits.
Tier B — Professional: license fee = USD 180k, 24/7 incident escalation, SLA-backed response times (4h P1), monthly minor upgrade windows, 250 ops credits included.
Tier C — Enterprise Resiliency: license fee = USD 350k+, dedicated technical account manager (TAM), custom upgrade cadence (customer-defined windows), 24/7 on-call, 1k ops credits, expedited security questionnaire service (QSA-assisted).
Ops credits: unit = 1 credit per physical maintenance hour or (soft) platform engineer labor; bundles sold in 100/250/1000 increments. Discounts scale with 2- and 3-year commitments. Prices are placeholders for experiment; legal pricing floors to be validated.
support_tiers:
Support definitions:
- Email & Knowledge Base: triage via support portal, target response P2: 2 business days.
- Escalation & Runbook Access: privileged logs and runbook sharing, P1 initial response target 4 hours, P2 8 hours.
- TAM & Warroom: dedicated TAM for Enterprise, quarterly business reviews, playbook-driven incident collaboration.
- Security Questionnaire Fast-track: pre-completed canonical SQ pack, mapping of answers to standard controls (SOC2, ISO), plus optional QSA engagement at Tier C.
upgrade_cadences:
Default cadence options for experiment:
- Quarterly (standard): security patches and minor releases in pre-announced quarterly windows with 7-day rollback window.
- Monthly (aggressive): for Professional tier customers requiring faster feature churn; compatibility SLAs and extra ops credits apply.
- Customer-controlled scheduling (Enterprise): customer selects 2 windows/year, Redwood provides hotfix channels between windows for critical fixes.
Each cadence includes a documented change window, maintenance SLA, and optional paid expedited upgrade outside windows.
acceptance_criteria: Documented pricing tiers and legal term template approved by Finance/Legal
SQ canonical pack created and validated with Security (mapping to SOC2/ISO controls)
Pilot agreement signed with 2 mid-enterprise customers using Tier B or C
Deal velocity metric shows >=10% improvement in pilot deals, with target 20% for success
Security review cycle time reduced by >=20% in pilot customers
risks: Legal: longer negotiation cycles if pricing floors not acceptable to customers
Engineering: delivering upgrade cadence SLAs requires on-call and release automation work (ENG-83422)
Security: canonical SQ pack may not satisfy some enterprise regulators without QSA involvement
Revenue: discounting to win pilots may set unwanted price expectations
runbook_and_rollout:
Phase 0: Align Finance/Legal/Security on pricing floors and SQ template (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Build canonical SQ pack and support playbooks; prepare Ops credit billing SKU and contract addenda (3 weeks).
Phase 2: Sales pilot with 2 targeted customers (6–10 weeks): collect metrics and feedback, track legal redlines and SQ rework time.
Phase 3: Post-pilot review: iterate pricing/support definitions and if successful, create GA packaging and sales enablement materials.
Playbooks, PRD, and contract template drafts live in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PP/OnPrem+Packaging+Experiment
